Hi @jonathf ,
I am unsure about the correct usage of chaospy.QoI_Dist(). Let's say I have an independent multivariate input distribution and a multidimensional function. I propagate the input distribution through the model via pseudospectral gPCE. I get an approximation of the function distribution in the form of a polynomial. So far so good. Now I want to take a look at the corresponding PDFs/CDFs of each output of my function by KDE using chaospy.QoI_Dist(). A sample code could look like this (chaospy version: 4.2.7 via pip):
import chaospy as chp
import numpy as np


dist_joint = chp.J(chp.Normal(mu=1000, sigma=100),
                   chp.Normal(mu=0.2, sigma=0.02))

dist_proxy = chp.Iid(chp.Normal(mu=0, sigma=1), 2)

poly = chp.orth_ttr(order=5, dist=dist_proxy)

nodes_proxy, weights_proxy = chp.generate_quadrature(order=5,
                                                     dist=dist_proxy,
                                                     rule='gaussian')

nodes_joint = dist_joint.inv(dist_proxy.fwd(nodes_proxy))

weights_joint = weights_proxy * dist_joint.pdf(nodes_joint) \
                / dist_proxy.pdf(nodes_proxy)

solves = np.zeros(shape=(nodes_joint[0].size, 3))
counter = 0
for ab in nodes_joint.T:
    solves[counter, :] = [ab[0], ab[1], ab[0] * ab[1]]
    counter += 1

approx = chp.fit_quadrature(orth=poly,
                            nodes=nodes_proxy,
                            weights=weights_joint,
                            solves=solves)

Now I want to construct the KDE. I figured out two possible ways, and I am unsure, which one is correct.

Constructing one KDE using approx directly:

dist_qoi = chp.QoI_Dist(poly=approx, dist=chp.Iid(chp.Normal(mu=0, sigma=1), 3))
This will result in a 3-dim distribution, where the H-matrix of the KDE is diagonal and I get stochastic dependency. Therefore pdf = dist_qoi[0].pdf(x) is possible whereas pdf = dist_qoi[1].pdf(x) for some x will result in the following error:
chaospy.StochasticallyDependentError: ItemDistribution(1, GaussianKDE()) has dangling dependencies.

Constructing separate KDE for each dimension of approx:

dist_qoi_1 = chp.QoI_Dist(poly=approx[0], dist=chp.Iid(chp.Normal(mu=0, sigma=1), 3))
dist_qoi_2 = chp.QoI_Dist(poly=approx[1], dist=chp.Iid(chp.Normal(mu=0, sigma=1), 3))

Here it is possible to obtain the corresponding PDFs/CDfs for each distribution, but the resulting graphs depend on the sampling distribution of chp.QoI_Dist, which should not be the case, if I am not mistaken. If this second approach is correct, do I need some transformation to obtain the "correct" distributions, i.e. which are independent of the kernel?
